reason: The text contains multiple explicit examples of Yahweh actively helping Jacob, the patriarch who becomes Israel. Key evidence includes: (1) God's direct command to Jacob to return to his ancestral homeland with the promise 'I will be with you' (Genesis 31:3); (2) God preventing Laban from harming Jacob despite Laban's hostile intentions (the divine warning in the dream not to speak to Jacob either good or bad); (3) Jacob's testimony that 'God did not allow him to harm me' and that 'God delivered the livestock of my father and gave it to me' (Genesis 31:7-9); (4) The angel of God appearing to Jacob in dreams to provide guidance and blessings; (5) Rachel and Leah's acknowledgment that 'God has rescued the wealth from our father...to us and to our children' (Genesis 31:16). These repeated interventions across the narrative demonstrate that assisting Jacob and preserving his welfare and prosperity are among Yahweh's demonstrated objectives. Since Jacob is the patriarch of the Hebrew people and the text emphasizes his descendants throughout, these divine actions toward Jacob represent God's commitment to helping the Hebrew people.
